lines:
Responsibilities: Executes explicit External Agent invocations through specialized lifecycle adapters, led by rich Codex App Server over local stdio and a generic ACP path. It negotiates and reports actual progress, native session, continuation, cancellation, approval-request, steering, artifact, and selected-MCP-forwarding capabilities; unsupported behavior is exposed and never simulated.
Owned runtime state: per-target negotiated ExternalAgentCapabilitySetV1, active invocation-to-native-session correlation, stdio/ACP request IDs, continuation cursor, pending external approval request, progress window, cancellation evidence, and health. Native session IDs are returned to core for normalized history; the cache is not canonical.
Versioned ports and contracts: ExternalAgentManifestV1, ExternalAgentStartV1, ExternalAgentContinueV1, ExternalAgentControlV1, ExternalApprovalRequestV1, ExternalAgentRawEventV1, NativeSessionRefV1, and ForwardableMcpSetV1. Continuation requires an approved envelope naming a retained native session and a declared continuation capability.
Failure and degraded behavior: missing features, native-session loss, protocol drift, opaque remote state, disconnect, cancel refusal, or process death is stated exactly. Killing a local client does not prove remote work stopped; an unconfirmed terminal state becomes uncertain and is never silently restarted.
Security and authority: the adapter cannot choose itself as a model fallback or new graph path, grant external approval, add MCP servers, expand workspace scope, or mint credentials. Approval requests return to the core authority boundary and resume only from a generation-fenced resolution.
Observability, performance, and cross-platform behavior: bounded progress streams, native/protocol correlation, latency/session/cancel metrics, opacity markers, redacted transcripts, and tested UTF-8 framing, path, argument, environment, and process-tree behavior on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
Non-responsibilities: no Aworkit Agent loop, MCP server semantics, workflow routing, authority/approval decisions, canonical transcript/history, retry policy, or hidden-reasoning reconstruction.

data.name: External Agent Adapter & Session Manager
data.technology: Rust adapter manager for Codex App Server stdio and ACP
